answers.text: Template again: delivery date, item and quantity, change from the order, in that order, three lines only. That's what keeps it the same each time.
Each claim gets a row — date, amount, category, submitter — then the total is just the sum at the bottom. Same layout every time.
The dates in that email don't line up — 14th to 19th but it's called three days out. I'd get that checked.
The delivery numbers, 54 to 62, look about right for the increase they mention.

I'd sign off Output 2, it shows the actual sales and returns numbers rather than just the percentage. You can't tell where Output 1's 4.1% came from, so it could be right but there's no way to check it from what's given.
Reply 2, it has references you can look up. Reply 1's claim that it won't happen again isn't backed by anything — though if someone checked it first, I don't see why it couldn't go out too.
1. No, that's the customer's own detail. 2. Yes. 3. No, not released yet. 4. Yes, that one's already public so it's fine. 5. No.
Pricing and discounts I'd hold back, and the confidentiality clause too because of the named parties. The rest I'm not sure, would check first.
I'd build in a step where a handful of the report's numbers get checked against the system, and I'd do that just before it goes up to my manager.
The bit where it reads the order email seems like the one to watch, since a mistake there could carry through.
